title: Neorealism (Italian art)
notes: Cited for: Neorealism rooted in the 1920s, suppressed by Fascist control, emerging after the regime fell; documentary-like objectivity with ordinary-looking actors.

title: The Bicycle Thief (film by De Sica [1948])
notes: Cited for: De Sica directed, Zavattini wrote; a poor man in postwar Rome whose bicycle, essential for his job, is stolen; non-professional actors Maggiorani and Staiola; on-location shooting.

title: Open City (film by Rossellini [1945])
notes: Cited for: shot months after the Allies liberated Rome, using rubble-strewn streets; many of the cast were not actors.

title: Rome, Open City: Roberto Rossellini's great leap for realism on screen
notes: Cited for: made on the streets of war-ravaged Rome with scraps of 35mm stock; won the Grand Prix at Cannes.

title: The Tribulations of the Working Class: Bicycle Thieves (Vittorio De Sica, 1948)
notes: Cited for: Antonio's job pasting posters requires a bicycle; De Sica drawn to Maggiorani's callused worker's hands.

title: New Wave (film)
notes: Cited for: individualistic French directors of the late 1950s associated with Cahiers du cinéma; showed films could be both commercial and artistic successes.

title: François Truffaut
notes: Cited for: eight years as a critic at Cahiers du cinéma; The 400 Blows won the best direction prize at Cannes 1959; the New Wave as a reaction against the tradition of quality.

title: The French New Wave Film That Changed American Cinema
notes: Cited for: Breathless shot handheld with low-budget guerrilla techniques, Coutard pushed in a wheelchair; jump cuts made by cutting within scenes.

title: Rashomon (film by Kurosawa [1950])
notes: Cited for: adapted from two Akutagawa stories; one event from conflicting perspectives; Golden Lion at Venice 1951; opened Western markets to Japanese film.

title: Kurosawa Akira
notes: Cited for: four persons recall a rape and a murder differently; cinema as a means of probing a metaphysical problem; first Japanese film to win such high international acclaim.

title: Akira Kurosawa Restorations
notes: Cited for: Italifilm president Giuliana Stramigioli recommended Rashomon to the Venice selection committee.

title: Ozu Yasujirō
notes: Cited for: originated the shomin-geki about lower-middle-class family life; almost totally abandoned camera movement for straight pictorial shots.

title: Tokyo Story: anatomy of a classic
notes: Cited for: an aged couple visit their children in Tokyo from Onomichi; fades and dissolves absent; tracking shots rare.

title: The enigmatic pillow shots of Yasujiro Ozu
notes: Cited for: low-angle framing as if seated on a tatami mat, a 50mm lens, minimal camera movement; pillow shots named by Noël Burch.

title: Satyajit Ray
notes: Cited for: advertising and book-design career; inspired by The Bicycle Thief and Jean Renoir; making Pather Panchali from 1952; Cannes 1956 award.

title: Pather Panchali (1955)
notes: Cited for: a boy growing up in an impoverished rural community; Apu and his sister run through a paddy field to glimpse a train; naturalistic portrait of ordinary lives.

title: Bollywood
notes: Cited for: Bombay plus Hollywood; Alam Ara (1931) first talkie; soundtracks and set pieces drive box office; playback singers and lip-syncing stars.

title: 10 great Bollywood musicals
notes: Cited for: Alam Ara advertised as all talking, all singing, all dancing, with seven song sequences; song and dance in every genre; playback singers.

title: Bleed, bleed, poor country: Shakespeare on the Indian screen
notes: Cited for: Parsi theatre flourished between the 1850s and 1930s and was a forerunner to Bollywood, combining folk and musical theatre traditions.

title: Lata Mangeshkar
notes: Cited for: iconic Indian playback singer who recorded songs for more than 2,000 Indian films.

title: Bruce Lee
notes: Cited for: The Big Boss and Fist of Fury; realistic martial arts; Enter the Dragon as the first Hong Kong and U.S. joint venture; died July 20, 1973.

title: Jackie Chan
notes: Cited for: Peking opera school training from age 7 to 17; bumbling physical comedy in 1978's Snake in the Eagle's Shadow and Drunken Master; own stunts, skull fracture on Armour of God.

title: Yuen Woo-ping: The Number One Martial Arts Director Under the Sky
notes: Cited for: born into a family of Peking Opera performers; directed Chan's 1978 hits; Hong Kong wirework in The Matrix changed Hollywood action.

title: Nollywood
notes: Cited for: naira devaluation and end of celluloid production; Living in Bondage (1992) straight to VHS; films shot in about a week; languages; the name in The New York Times in 2002.

title: Venice Film Festival
notes: Cited for: founded 1932, part of the Venice Biennale, the world's oldest film festival; the Golden Lion.

title: Cannes film festival
notes: Cited for: first held in 1946; became an international marketplace where producers and distributors view films and sign contracts.

title: The history of the Festival
notes: Cited for (the festival's own history): Erlanger's idea of a festival free of pressure; planned opening on 1 September 1939; first held 1946; first Palme d'Or 1955; Marché du Film official in 1959.

title: Auditorium Louis Lumière
publisher: Palais des Festivals et des Congrès de Cannes
notes: Cited for (the venue's own page): the Grand Auditorium bears the name of Louis Lumière and hosts the Festival de Cannes ceremonies.
